lessons.seo_title: Linear Equations from Shopping — Grade 9 Worked Examples
lessons.thumbnail_angle: See the objects. Solve the equation.
lessons.real_world_hook: Three apples cost twelve dollars. What does one apple cost?
lessons.concept_intuition: Three apples have the same price. Together they cost twelve dollars. Let p be the price of one apple.
lessons.visual_hints: Use the exact authored visual data in the lesson design.
lessons.common_mistake: Subtract three from twelve to find the unit price. Three is the number of equal groups. Divide twelve by three.

lessons.seo_title: Quadratic Area Models — Grade 10 Worked Examples
lessons.thumbnail_angle: See the objects. Solve the equation.
lessons.real_world_hook: A polynomial can encode an area. Arrange the pieces and its factors become side lengths.
lessons.concept_intuition: One square x-squared tile, five x-tiles, and six unit tiles can form a rectangle.
lessons.visual_hints: Use the exact authored visual data in the lesson design.
lessons.common_mistake: The roots of (x+2)(x+3)=0 are 2 and 3. Each factor must equal zero, giving negative 2 and negative 3.
